title: Your Life as Cornelius Vanderbilt | $100 to America's Richest

scenes.text: It's January 1867, and snow is falling on the Hudson River at Albany.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: You own the railroad that runs from here to New York City.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: And this morning, you've ordered your trains to stop at the river.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: Thousands of passengers from the West are stuck in the snow, with nowhere to go.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: Your rival's railroad has just become worthless, and everyone knows who did it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: You started with a hundred dollars borrowed from your mother.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: a small two-masted flat-bottomed sailing ferry (periauger) crossing New York harbor, 1810: choppy water, Manhattan's low skyline and church steeples, gulls

scenes.text: When you die, you'll be the richest man in America, worth about a hundred million dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Within a few generations, almost all of it will be gone.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By the end, you'll know the one money rule that made you,
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: and whether it still works today.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But to get here, we have to go back. It's 1794, on Staten Island, New York.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: You're born on May 27th, in a farmhouse by the water. Your name is Cornelius.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: Your father farms, and ferries vegetables to Manhattan in a small boat.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: Your mother, Phebe, is the one who handles the money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: Family legend says she keeps the savings hidden in the old grandfather clock.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: Keep count of three things: the money, your enemies, and your thirteen children.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: You quit school at eleven. You'll never read or write well. Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: Instead, you work on your father's boat, and you learn the harbor like a map.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: a small two-masted flat-bottomed sailing ferry (periauger) crossing New York harbor, 1810: choppy water, Manhattan's low skyline and church steeples, gulls

scenes.text: You also learn that you hate to lose. At anything.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: a small two-masted flat-bottomed sailing ferry (periauger) crossing New York harbor, 1810: choppy water, Manhattan's low skyline and church steeples, gulls

scenes.text: You race other boys, on horses and on boats, and you usually win.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: a small two-masted flat-bottomed sailing ferry (periauger) crossing New York harbor, 1810: choppy water, Manhattan's low skyline and church steeples, gulls

scenes.text: That temper, too. Remember it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: a small two-masted flat-bottomed sailing ferry (periauger) crossing New York harbor, 1810: choppy water, Manhattan's low skyline and church steeples, gulls

scenes.text: In 1810, you're sixteen, and you want your own boat.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: The family story goes that your mother makes you a deal.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: Clear and plant eight acres of rocky land by your birthday, and she'll lend you a hundred dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: You get your friends to help, and finish in time.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: With the hundred dollars, you buy a periauger: a flat-bottomed sailboat with two masts.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: a small two-masted flat-bottomed sailing ferry (periauger) crossing New York harbor, 1810: choppy water, Manhattan's low skyline and church steeples, gulls

scenes.text: You ferry people and goods between Staten Island and Manhattan, for eighteen cents a trip.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: a small two-masted flat-bottomed sailing ferry (periauger) crossing New York harbor, 1810: choppy water, Manhattan's low skyline and church steeples, gulls

scenes.text: You sail in weather the other boatmen won't touch.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: a small two-masted flat-bottomed sailing ferry (periauger) crossing New York harbor, 1810: choppy water, Manhattan's low skyline and church steeples, gulls

scenes.text: Within a year, the story goes, you pay your mother back and hand her a thousand dollars more.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Port Richmond, Staten Island, 1800s: small Dutch farmhouse with a stone chimney, vegetable fields, a wooden dock, sailboats on the Kill Van Kull, morning

scenes.text: In time, other captains start calling you the Commodore, as a joke. The name sticks.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The snowy day you stop the trains is fifty-seven years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: During the War of 1812, you win a contract to carry supplies to the forts around the harbor.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: a small two-masted flat-bottomed sailing ferry (periauger) crossing New York harbor, 1810: choppy water, Manhattan's low skyline and church steeples, gulls

scenes.text: In 1813, you marry your cousin, Sophia Johnson. You're both teenagers.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You'll have thirteen children. Keep counting.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By 1817, you own several sailing ships and about nine thousand dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Then something new appears on the water: the steamboat.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: It doesn't need wind. You realize sailing is finished.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: So you do something strange for a rich young captain: you sell your ships and take a job.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: You become captain of a steamboat called the Bellona, for a man named Thomas Gibbons.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: You want to learn the steam business from the inside, with someone else's money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: There's one problem: running steamboats in New York waters is illegal.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: The state has given a monopoly to the heirs of Robert Fulton and Robert Livingston.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: A monopoly: the only company allowed to sell something, so it can charge what it likes.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: Gibbons doesn't care. Neither do you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: You run your boat cheaper than theirs, and when sheriffs come to arrest you, you hide.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: Legend says you built a secret compartment on board to hide in. You usually just outran them.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: deck of a small paddle-wheel steamboat on New York Bay, 1818: smokestack with black smoke, wooden paddle box, passengers in top hats and bonnets, rail and rope

scenes.text: Sophia runs an inn at the New Brunswick landing, called Bellona Hall.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bellona Hall inn in New Brunswick, New Jersey, 1820: a busy tavern dining room, long tables, fireplace, travelers with luggage, a counter with ledgers

scenes.text: Travelers sleep and eat there between your boat and the stagecoach to Philadelphia.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bellona Hall inn in New Brunswick, New Jersey, 1820: a busy tavern dining room, long tables, fireplace, travelers with luggage, a counter with ledgers

scenes.text: She's earning money while raising your growing pile of children. Remember her.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bellona Hall inn in New Brunswick, New Jersey, 1820: a busy tavern dining room, long tables, fireplace, travelers with luggage, a counter with ledgers

scenes.text: Gibbons takes the monopoly all the way to the Supreme Court.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the US Supreme Court chamber in the Capitol basement, 1824: vaulted ceiling, semicircle of judges' chairs, black-robed justices, lawyers at tables, candles

scenes.text: The case is called Gibbons versus Ogden.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the US Supreme Court chamber in the Capitol basement, 1824: vaulted ceiling, semicircle of judges' chairs, black-robed justices, lawyers at tables, candles

scenes.text: Chief Justice John Marshall rules that only Congress can regulate trade between the states.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the US Supreme Court chamber in the Capitol basement, 1824: vaulted ceiling, semicircle of judges' chairs, black-robed justices, lawyers at tables, candles

scenes.text: Commerce, he writes, is traffic, but it is something more.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the US Supreme Court chamber in the Capitol basement, 1824: vaulted ceiling, semicircle of judges' chairs, black-robed justices, lawyers at tables, candles

quote.text: Commerce, undoubtedly, is traffic, but it is something more.

scenes.text: The monopoly is dead. The water is open to anyone.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the US Supreme Court chamber in the Capitol basement, 1824: vaulted ceiling, semicircle of judges' chairs, black-robed justices, lawyers at tables, candles

scenes.text: And nobody knows how to run a cheap steamboat better than you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the US Supreme Court chamber in the Capitol basement, 1824: vaulted ceiling, semicircle of judges' chairs, black-robed justices, lawyers at tables, candles

scenes.text: In 1829, you leave Gibbons and start your own steamboat line.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: two paddle steamboats racing side by side on the Hudson River, 1830s: thick smoke, cliffs of the Palisades, passengers crowding the rails, bright day

scenes.text: Your weapon is always the same: a lower price.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: two paddle steamboats racing side by side on the Hudson River, 1830s: thick smoke, cliffs of the Palisades, passengers crowding the rails, bright day

scenes.text: Here's how a fare war works.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Imagine two coffee carts on the same corner, both charging two dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You cut your price to one dollar. Every customer walks to you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You barely make a profit, but your rival makes nothing at all.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You can survive this because your costs are lower: cheaper fuel, cheaper crews, tighter ships.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Soon your rival has two choices: go broke, or pay you to leave the corner.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Either way, you win. Customers win too, until the war is over.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: On the Hudson, you cut the fare from Albany to New York to almost nothing.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: two paddle steamboats racing side by side on the Hudson River, 1830s: thick smoke, cliffs of the Palisades, passengers crowding the rails, bright day

scenes.text: Some days, you carry passengers for free and sell them dinner on board.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: two paddle steamboats racing side by side on the Hudson River, 1830s: thick smoke, cliffs of the Palisades, passengers crowding the rails, bright day

scenes.text: The big Hudson River steamboat owners can't take it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: two paddle steamboats racing side by side on the Hudson River, 1830s: thick smoke, cliffs of the Palisades, passengers crowding the rails, bright day

scenes.text: So they pay you about a hundred thousand dollars, plus five thousand a year, to go away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You take it, and go fight on another river.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Critics call it blackmail. You call it a business model.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By the mid-1840s, you're a millionaire.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The snowy day you stop the trains is twenty-one years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: At home, things are colder.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You move the family into a big house on Washington Place, in Manhattan. Sophia doesn't want to go.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When she resists and falls into depression, you have her committed to an asylum.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The woman who ran Bellona Hall for you spends months locked away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You're not much kinder to your son William, whom everyone calls Billy.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You think he's slow, and you send him to run a farm on Staten Island.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Billy. Remember him.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1848, gold is found in California, and everyone wants to get there fast.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By land, it takes months. By sea around South America, months more.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Most people cross at Panama, through the jungle.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You pick a route through Nicaragua instead: shorter by hundreds of miles.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: Your boats go up the San Juan River, across Lake Nicaragua, then a coach ride to the Pacific.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: You go yourself, and push a steamboat up the rapids personally. You're fifty-six.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: And of course, you charge less than Panama.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: Soon your Accessory Transit Company is carrying thousands of gold-seekers a year.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: In 1853, you take a break. You build a giant yacht, the North Star, and sail to Europe.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: grand saloon of the steam yacht North Star, 1853: carved rosewood panels, velvet sofas, chandeliers, portholes showing the sea

scenes.text: You tell a newspaper you're worth about eleven million dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: grand saloon of the steam yacht North Star, 1853: carved rosewood panels, velvet sofas, chandeliers, portholes showing the sea

scenes.text: While you're away, your partners Charles Morgan and Cornelius Garrison take control of the company.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: grand saloon of the steam yacht North Star, 1853: carved rosewood panels, velvet sofas, chandeliers, portholes showing the sea

scenes.text: When you come home, the money's moving into their pockets, not yours.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: This is where you write the most famous business letter in America.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Gentlemen: You have undertaken to cheat me. I won't sue you, for the law is too slow. I'll ruin you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: I WON'T SUE YOU. I'LL RUIN YOU.

scenes.text: Except, the historian T. J. Stiles found no evidence you ever wrote it. It appears decades later.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: What you really do is just as brutal. You start a rival line and undercut them.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: Then it gets stranger.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: An American adventurer named William Walker invades Nicaragua with a small army and makes himself president.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: In 1856, Walker cancels your company's rights and gives them to your partners.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: So you help fund Walker's enemies, and send your own agent to Costa Rica.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: In 1857, Walker's army is beaten. You've helped overthrow a government to win a business dispute.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: river steamer on the San Juan River in Nicaragua, 1851: dense jungle banks, rapids, gold rush travelers with carpet bags, a volcano in the distance, humid haze

scenes.text: Then the big Panama steamship lines pay you to stop competing. Again.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1861, the Civil War begins.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You give the Union Navy your biggest steamship, the Vanderbilt, worth hundreds of thousands of dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Congress thanks you with a gold medal.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But your youngest son, George, falls ill while serving in the army, and dies in 1864.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You're about to turn seventy. Most rich men retire. You switch industries.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Ships are yesterday. You think railroads are tomorrow.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You start buying the New York and Harlem Railroad, a small line everyone thinks is junk.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Some city politicians try to make money by selling Harlem stock short.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Selling short: selling shares you don't own yet, betting you can buy them back cheaper later.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So you quietly buy up almost every share in existence.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When the short sellers have to buy shares to pay back, you're the only seller left.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The price shoots past a hundred dollars a share. They're ruined.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Then you buy the Hudson River Railroad too. Now you own both lines into New York City.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You make Billy, the son you called slow, your vice president. He turns out to be very good at it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Which brings us back to that snowy morning in Albany.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: The New York Central Railroad runs from Buffalo to Albany. Your lines carry its passengers to the city.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: The Central's owners have been playing games with you on the deals.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: So you stop your trains at the river. Nobody connects to the Central anymore.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: Passengers and freight pile up in the snow. The Central's stock price collapses.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky

scenes.text: By the end of 1867, the Central's shareholders beg you to take over. You do.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Now you control the road from New York City all the way to Buffalo and the Great Lakes.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But one railroad still competes with you: the Erie.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You start buying Erie shares to take it over.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Its directors, Daniel Drew, Jay Gould, and Jim Fisk, have a better idea.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: They print new Erie shares, as fast as you can buy them.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Fisk jokes: if this printing press don't break down, I'll give the old hog all he wants of Erie.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: If this printing press don't break down, I'll give the old hog all he wants of Erie.

scenes.text: The old hog is you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A judge you're friendly with orders their arrest. They flee across the river to Jersey City.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: They take millions of dollars of your cash with them, in bundles.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: After months of lawsuits and bribed lawmakers on both sides, you settle.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You get most of your money back, and you leave the Erie alone.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You've finally lost a race. It doesn't happen often.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1868, Sophia dies. A year later, you're seventy-five and married again.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your new wife, Frank Crawford, is a cousin from Alabama, about forty-five years younger.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Yes, her name is Frank. And yes, she's a woman.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Now remember the Erie men printing shares? You do something similar.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You merge your railroads and issue tens of millions in new stock, backed by nothing new.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It's called watered stock, after cattle fed water before they're weighed at market.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Mark Twain writes you an open letter, mocking your worship of money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Go and surprise the whole country, he says, by doing something right.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: Go and surprise the whole country by doing something right.

scenes.text: You also become a believer in spiritualism: talking to the dead.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Two of your mediums, Victoria Woodhull and her sister Tennessee Claflin, open a stockbroker's office with your backing.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: They're the first women to run a brokerage firm on Wall Street. The press is scandalized.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1871, you open Grand Central Depot in Manhattan.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Grand Central Depot in New York, 1871: vast iron-and-glass train shed, steam locomotives, gas lamps, crowds with luggage, a big clock

scenes.text: It's one of the biggest buildings in the country. Today, your bronze statue stands outside its replacement.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Grand Central Depot in New York, 1871: vast iron-and-glass train shed, steam locomotives, gas lamps, crowds with luggage, a big clock

scenes.text: The Panic of 1873 crashes Wall Street. You calmly keep building.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember the boy who quit school at eleven?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That year, you give a million dollars to a college in Nashville, Tennessee.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A Methodist bishop married to Frank's cousin has asked you to help unite the North and South after the war.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You write that you hope it helps strengthen the ties between all sections of our common country.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: ...strengthening the ties which should exist between all sections of our common country.

scenes.text: They rename it Vanderbilt University. It's the biggest gift you ever give.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By 1876, you're eighty-two, sick, and in pain.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Reporters camp outside your house on Washington Place for months, waiting.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: On January 4th, 1877, you die at home.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You're the richest man in America. Your fortune: about a hundred million dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That's more than two billion dollars today, in a much smaller economy.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your will leaves about ninety million dollars to just one child.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Billy. The slow son you sent to the farm.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your daughters get small shares. Two of your children sue.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: At trial, the family's secrets, including the séances and Sophia's asylum, end up in the newspapers.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Billy settles, and then doubles the fortune in eight years. You were wrong about him.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So how did the richest man in America leave a fortune that disappeared?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Billy's children build palaces: The Breakers, Biltmore, a row of mansions on Fifth Avenue.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Nobody in the family builds a new business. Everybody spends.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Myth time: you're often quoted saying, the public be damned.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That wasn't you. It was Billy, to a reporter, in 1882.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1973, about a hundred and twenty members of your family hold a reunion at Vanderbilt University.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Grand Central Depot in New York, 1871: vast iron-and-glass train shed, steam locomotives, gas lamps, crowds with luggage, a big clock

scenes.text: By one family historian's count, not one of them is a millionaire.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Grand Central Depot in New York, 1871: vast iron-and-glass train shed, steam locomotives, gas lamps, crowds with luggage, a big clock

scenes.text: Here's the money rule.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The rule: whoever can do the job for less can afford to win the price war.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Today it's budget airlines: no free meals, packed seats, cheap fares, huge profits.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And it works for a household too. Cut two hundred dollars of monthly costs, and that's twenty-four hundred a year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A raise you give yourself, with no new boss.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But here's where the rule failed. Once you won, you raised prices and watered stock.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Customers only win the price war while it lasts.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And your heirs never learned the rule. They learned to spend.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A cheap boat can beat a big one. A big fortune can't survive a lazy heir.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: East Albany rail yard on the Hudson River, January 1867: snow falling, stopped steam locomotives and passenger cars, frozen river, crowds with luggage, grey sky
scenes.title: YOUR LIFE AS CORNELIUS VANDERBILT

meta.thumbnail: You, white-whiskered in a black frock coat, standing in front of a snow-stopped locomotive with arms crossed; text: '$100 TO $100M'
meta.description:
You borrow $100 from your mother at 16 and buy a sailboat.
You die the richest man in America. Then your family spends it all.

A comedic dramatization of documented history.

Sources:
T. J. Stiles, The First Tycoon: The Epic Life of Cornelius Vanderbilt (2009)
Arthur T. Vanderbilt II, Fortune's Children (1989)
Gibbons v. Ogden, 22 U.S. 1 (1824)
Mark Twain, 'Open Letter to Com. Vanderbilt', Packard's Monthly (March 1869)
factCheck: Born 27 May 1794, Port Richmond, Staten Island; parents Cornelius van Derbilt and Phebe Hand (Stiles)
Grandfather-clock savings and 8-acre loan deal are family stories, flagged as legend in script (Stiles; Lane, Commodore Vanderbilt 1942)
Left school ~age 11; limited literacy (Stiles)
Bought periauger 1810 with $100 from mother; ferry fare 18 cents; repaid plus ~$1,000 within a year (family accounts, Stiles)
'Commodore' nickname from young age; War of 1812 harbor-fort supply contract
Married cousin Sophia Johnson Dec 1813; 13 children
~$9,000 by 1817; captain of Gibbons's Bellona from 1818 (Stiles)
Fulton-Livingston steam monopoly in NY waters; Vanderbilt evaded arrest; Gibbons v. Ogden decided 2 March 1824, opinion by Marshall
Sophia ran Bellona Hall, New Brunswick NJ
Own line from 1829; Hudson River Association paid ~$100,000 plus $5,000/yr to withdraw (mid-1830s; Stiles)
Millionaire by mid-1840s (~$1.2M estimated 1846)
Moved to 10 Washington Place ~1846; Sophia committed to Bloomingdale Asylum ~1846-47 (Stiles)
William Henry sent to Staten Island farm; thought dull by father
Gold Rush; Accessory Transit Company Nicaragua route from 1851; Vanderbilt personally piloted a steamer up the San Juan rapids, age 56-57
North Star grand tour 1853; told press fortune ~$11M; Morgan and Garrison took control of Transit
'I'll ruin you' letter: Stiles found no contemporary evidence; first printed decades later (The First Tycoon, notes)
William Walker seized Nicaragua 1855-56, revoked Transit charter Feb 1856; Vanderbilt backed Costa Rica, agent Sylvanus Spencer; Walker surrendered May 1857
Donated steamship Vanderbilt to Union 1862 (valued ~$800,000); Congressional gold medal/joint resolution of thanks 1864
Son George Washington Vanderbilt died 1864 of illness contracted in service
Harlem corner 1863-64: price rose from under $10 (1862) to over $100 (Stiles)
Hudson River Railroad control 1864; William Henry vice president
New York Central blockade at East Albany, January 1867; control of Central by Dec 1867
Erie War 1868 with Drew, Gould, Fisk; Fisk 'printing press' quote widely reported; directors fled to Jersey City with ~$7M; settlement July 1868, Vanderbilt recovered most losses
Sophia died Aug 1868; married Frank Armstrong Crawford Aug 1869 (she ~30, he 75)
Consolidation Nov 1869 with ~$23M stock dividend ('watered stock')
Twain open letter, Packard's Monthly, March 1869
Backed Woodhull, Claflin & Co., first women-run Wall Street brokerage, Feb 1870
Grand Central Depot opened 1871; statue at St. John's Park freight depot 1869
Panic of 1873; $1M gift to Central University, Nashville, 1873 via Bishop Holland McTyeire (Frank's cousin), renamed Vanderbilt University
Died 4 Jan 1877 at 10 Washington Place, age 82; fortune ~$100M; richest man in America at the time (Stiles); ~$2.9B today via CPI x ~29 (1877-2026); as share of GDP far larger
Will left ~$90M+ to William Henry; contested by Cornelia and Cornelius Jeremiah; settled 1879
William Henry roughly doubled fortune to ~$200M by his death in 1885
'The public be damned': William Henry Vanderbilt, 1882 interview, Chicago Daily News
1973 family reunion at Vanderbilt University, ~120 descendants, no millionaire among them (Arthur T. Vanderbilt II, Fortune's Children)
Household example numbers are illustrative arithmetic
sources: T. J. Stiles, The First Tycoon (Knopf, 2009)
John Marshall, Gibbons v. Ogden, 22 U.S. 1 (1824): 'Commerce, undoubtedly, is traffic, but it is something more: it is intercourse.' https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/22/1
Jim Fisk 'printing press... old hog' quote: reported in Charles Francis Adams Jr., 'A Chapter of Erie' (1869) and Stiles
Mark Twain, 'Open Letter to Com. Vanderbilt', Packard's Monthly, March 1869
Vanderbilt letter to Holland McTyeire, 1873, Vanderbilt University history: https://www.vanderbilt.edu/about/history/
Arthur T. Vanderbilt II, Fortune's Children: The Fall of the House of Vanderbilt (1989)
